extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, Congress, General Land Office officials, miners and other stakeholders in federal mineral land policy
extracted.subtask_description: Federal policy proposals for turning public mineral lands into a revenue source: registering and confirming existing miners' claims, adopting a geodetic survey system, subdividing mineral lands into one-acre tracts, and setting pricing/licensing and sale procedures to attract investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mineral lands as a source of national revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: The mineral lands of the public domain ought to yield a national revenue; our mineral riches justify using them as a revenue source in the present condition of the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument and evidence provided: enormous discoveries of gold, silver, quicksilver, tin, copper, lead, iron, and coal; large annual yields historically and since California; estimate of public mineral lands exceeding twenty million acres; these lands are public property and in present circumstances ought to be made a source of revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary reconnoissance and licensing (proposed $10 license)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a preliminary reconnoissance and charge licenses (proposed at $10 each) to be paid in the meantime by miners to the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the Commissioner's preliminary proposal; the license fee would fund an initial reconnaissance and is an interim measure before more comprehensive policy or sale procedures are implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require registration, survey-notes, and production reporting by present miners
rubrics_metrics.description: Present miners working these lands without legal title should be required to register their claims with the proper officer of the Federal Government, to file copies and descriptive notes of their surveys and locations, and to report the product of the mines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: to form a basis for Government reconnoissance and exploration, to prevent litigation among present miners, to enable the Government to separate their lands from the public domain and to give them a perfect title, and to allow resurvey and official documentation of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm existing miners' rights under local regulations and issue titles at nominal cost
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be just and good policy to confirm the rights of the present miners according to the existing regulations in the several districts, charging them only a nominal price for a complete title and patent from the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominal price should not exceed the cost of survey and incidental expenses (only a few cents an acre). This confirmation would improve miners' condition, give them perfect title where now they have none, and in many cases enable them to raise capital for more profitable working.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant present miners fee-simple title without rent, regie, or seigniorage
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the present occupants certain title in fee simple, without rent, regie, or seigniorage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is proposed as a way to stabilize miners' holdings and encourage investment; contrasted with current situation where no title can be acquired and capital is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide the policy problem into survey/subdivision and price/mode of sale
rubrics_metrics.description: The solution to making mineral lands a revenue source divides itself into two parts: (1) the survey and subdivision of these lands; and (2) the price and mode of sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing device to separate technical surveying/subdivision issues from economic/pricing policy; subsequent recommendations address each part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt the geodetic survey system (instead of purely linear surveys)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the geodetic system for surveys because errors in linear surveys are much greater than in geodetic, especially in minute subdivisions; geodetic surveys provide interior information and maps enabling Government appraisal of every acre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons: (1) linear survey errors unacceptable for minute (acre) subdivisions; (2) geodetic system informs interior and enables appraisal and proper maps similar to coast survey; (3) additional cost would hardly reach two cents an acre. Also: continue present mode of townships/sections with further subdivisions but overlay geodetic precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdivide gold and silver lands into one-acre tracts
rubrics_metrics.description: The subdivision of the gold and silver lands should be into tracts of one acre each, continuing and extending the present system of townships and sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed procedural scheme provided: break quarter-quarter (40-acre) tracts into two 20-acre-like splits into 10-acre tracts, then into 5-acre tracts, then into five 1-acre tracts by further lines. The textual diagram and dimensions (110 yards by 44 yards per 1-acre tract sides) specify the method and assert this is the only practicable plan to reach one-acre tracts under the existing township/section framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specified dimensions for one-acre tract layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Each one-acre tract would have exterior east-west lines of 110 yards (330 feet) and north-south sides of 44 yards (132 feet) according to the proposed subdivision layout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text provides a diagram and exact yard/foot measures for the proposed one-acre tracts, and explains why square-acre subdivisions are impracticable given existing section shapes; this is part of the technical specification for subdivision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark exterior survey lines with monuments at set intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark by stone or iron monuments the north and south exterior lines of each section at intervals of forty-four yards, and the east and west lines at distances of one hundred and ten yards, to complete the survey extending from section to section and township to township.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This marking regime is presented as the necessary field implementation detail to carry out the one-acre subdivision plan and ensure continuous, unambiguous boundaries across townships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sell unoccupied mineral lands at proper market value to attract foreign capital
rubrics_metrics.description: For the vast unoccupied public mineral domain, provide title for new mines at their proper value and thus bring in foreign capital to invest in working our mines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: current inability to acquire title limits capital investment; selling at proper value and providing certainty of title will accelerate development of mineral wealth. This criterion connects pricing/sale policy to broader economic development goals such as attracting investment and accelerating exploitation of resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make survey detail sufficient to allow government appraisal of each acre
rubrics_metrics.description: Use survey methods and maps (geodetic) that enable the Government to appraise every acre and give proper maps similar to those of the coast survey so the people can judge the value of each acre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the appraisal/information objective: accurate interior surveys and maps are needed so the government can set values and inform potential buyers/investors; the small extra cost is justified by these benefits.
